name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development-Skeletal Anomalies Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with discordant phenotypic sex
Presence of congenital skeletal anomalies including limb malformations and vertebral defects
Ambiguous or atypical external genitalia inconsistent with 46,XX karyotype
Abnormal endocrine profile consistent with disorder of sex development
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with sex development and skeletal formation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with discordant phenotypic sex plus congenital skeletal anomalies and ambiguous genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and genetic; multidisciplinary evaluation recommended

laboratory: Abnormal serum hormone levels including elevated androgens
imaging: Radiographic evidence of limb malformations and vertebral anomalies
Pelvic ultrasound showing atypical internal reproductive structures
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as SOX9, NR5A1, or others involved in sex development and skeletal formation
other: Histopathological examination of gonadal tissue may show dysgenesis

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Normal to elevated androgen levels with resistance
Severe skeletal dysplasia with bowed long bones
Respiratory compromise due to thoracic hypoplasia

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth in 46,XX individual
Severe skeletal malformations compromising mobility or respiration
Rapid onset of adrenal crisis or electrolyte imbalance
references: Orphanet: 46,XX difference of sex development-skeletal anomalies syndrome - ORPHA:2975
Lee PA, et al. Disorders of Sex Development. Endocrinol Metab Clin North Am. 2015
Muller J, et al. Skeletal anomalies in 46,XX DSD: clinical and molecular insights. Am J Med Genet A. 2022
